steps.prompt: Two numbers add up to $30$ and differ by $8$. What are they? How did you find them?
steps.placeholder: The numbers are… I found them by…

cards.title: Two unknowns, two equations
cards.body: With two unknowns you need two equations. Elimination: add or subtract the equations so one letter cancels. Substitution: solve one equation for a letter and put that into the other. Pick whichever makes a letter vanish fastest.

cards.title: Worked example: add to eliminate
cards.problem: Two numbers add up to $30$ and differ by $8$. What are they?

steps.text: Write the two equations: $x + y = 30$ and $x - y = 8$.
Add them: the $y$'s cancel and $2x = 38$, so $x = 19$.
Put $x = 19$ back into $x + y = 30$ to find $y$.

cards.title: Find what is asked, not always $x$ and $y$
cards.body: AMC questions often ask for $x + y$ or $x - y$, and you can get it in one step. If $3x + 2y = 17$ and $2x + 3y = 13$, adding gives $5x + 5y = 30$, so $x + y = 6$ without ever finding $x$ or $y$. Look at the question before you start solving.

cards.title: Worked example: tickets
cards.problem: Adult tickets cost $\$8$ and child tickets $\$5$. A show sold $40$ tickets for $\$266$. How many adult tickets were sold?

steps.text: Let $a$ be adult tickets. Then $40 - a$ are child tickets, and $8a + 5(40 - a) = 266$.

cards.title: The common trap: stopping halfway
cards.body: After finding one letter, check which one the question wants, and put your answer into BOTH equations to check it. Also, two equations don't always give one answer: $x + y = 5$ and $2x + 2y = 7$ have none (the lines are parallel), and $x + y = 5$ and $2x + 2y = 10$ have infinitely many.

prompts: When a question asks for $x + y$, what will you try before solving for $x$ and $y$?
